forces.title: Specialised retail channels boost Tobacco Products sales in Ireland
forces.description: Amidst a challenging Irish retail environment, specialised stores focusing on Food, Beverages & Tobacco are experiencing stronger performance. This trend suggests sustained consumer demand for tobacco products sold through these specific retail channels. Manufacturers and distributors of tobacco products can leverage this channel strength to maintain sales volumes and potentially grow market share, mitigating the impact of broader retail slowdowns and cost-of-living pressures on consumer spending.

forces.title: New EU packaging rules mandate product range alterations for producers
forces.description: EU Regulation 2025/40, effective August 2026, aims to reduce packaging waste, enhance recycling, and improve label clarity across the EU. This legislation will necessitate changes to packaging for all producers, including those in the Tobacco Products sector. Tobacco manufacturers will need to invest in redesigning and altering their product ranges' packaging to comply, representing a structural shift in operational requirements and potentially increasing compliance costs.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Food and Drink Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

viewpoints.title: Irish specialised stores for Food, Beverages & Tobacco show stronger performance
viewpoints.description: Ireland's retail sector faces a challenging trading environment, with overall sales volumes declining. However, specialised stores specifically catering to 'Food, Beverages & Tobacco' have demonstrated stronger performance, indicating resilience. This suggests that consumer demand for these specific categories, including tobacco products, remains robust within this segment, potentially buffering manufacturers and distributors from broader retail downturns influenced by cost-of-living pressures.
